Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class X509ChainCustomizer

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.X509ChainCustomizer
All Implemented Interfaces:
LoginChainCustomizer
public class X509ChainCustomizer extends Object implements LoginChainCustomizer
Adds the sign-in with a client certificate to the login/UI chain through http.x509(...). The filter only looks at POST /login/x509, the form of X509LoginMethodFragment on the login page, which carries the CSRF token like every other form of the chain; the CSRF filter runs before the X.509 one, so a cross-site page can never make a browser sign in with its certificate. The form posts to the TLS port that requests a certificate (or to the proxy that forwards one); every other request of the chain is untouched, and GET /login/x509 is not a sign-in at all (it is not opened, so it ends with the chain's catch-all rule). A certificate that is bound to an account signs it in and resumes the interrupted request, anything else goes back to the login page. The path is open to everybody, because it is where the certificate is checked. When a proxy may forward the certificate, ForwardedCertificateFilter runs first. Once the chain is configured, the success handler gets the chain's session authentication strategy, the one the form login uses.
